description:
Stop worktrees sharing Cargo build state through hardlinks from the cache pool.

## Background

`.agents/skills/jit-execution-lead/scripts/dispatch-worker-worktree.sh:97` seeds a worktree's target with `cp -al`, so a build script's `output` file is one inode across sibling worktrees and the pool. Cargo rewrites that file in place. A sibling's build then writes its digest into another worktree's build state (`f61ad6362` records the two-checkout reproduction). The fallback `cp -au` in `reclaim-worker-worktree.sh` can write through a shared inode the same way, unlike its `rsync` branch. Slots seeded the old way keep the shared inodes until reseeded.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: After seeding, no file under a directory named `build`, no `*.d` file, and no file or directory entry whose name starts with `.`, at any depth, shares an inode with the pool. The remaining entries stay hardlinked.
- [hard] REQ-02: Both harvest branches of `reclaim-worker-worktree.sh` replace destination files instead of writing through them.
- [hard] REQ-03: A test over the dispatch script fails on the old `cp -al` seed and passes on the new one.
- [hard] REQ-04: The issue records that the two-checkout reproduction no longer reproduces on the new seed, whether anything under `deps/` is written in place, and that a worktree seeded from the current pool builds correctly.





## Evidence

Final seed at `2d09f45d3`, on two fresh dispatches. Scope: `cargo build -p jit` plus `cargo test -p jit --test cli_gate --no-run`, with `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`; narrowed from the workspace because of disk.

- Reproduction does not reproduce: Y built digest `ea234764`, sibling X then built `27a8c7d8`, and Y's `output` kept its digest, inode and mtime, matched a recomputation from Y's source, and stayed Fresh.
- Concurrent edit-and-build: 29.9 s and 30.4 s, against about 28.6 s alone, so not serialized.
- In-place writes: on an earlier new-style seed (`689e329de`), with `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, a `-p jit` build and a test build changed 0 hardlinked files in place. On a throwaway crate with incremental on, 0 of 152 hardlinked files changed in place, 139 of them under `incremental/`; plain `cp -al` as the control gave 19.
- A seed from the current pool builds correctly: only `jit` recompiled, and its digest matched a recomputation. The pool's `deps/jit-69ec36a944bfff87.d` names a deleted scratch path and did not affect these builds; it stays in place.
- Seed cost: about 1355 MiB per seed, 0 inodes in the rule classes shared with the pool.
title: Worktrees seeded from the cache pool share no Cargo build state
